standard.title: Area and Perimeter of Composite Shapes
standard.description: solve problems involving the area and perimeter of irregular and composite shapes using appropriate units
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply area formulas for triangles, rectangles and parallelograms (from AC9M7M01). Students can calculate circumference of circles (from AC9M7M03).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students decompose or compose irregular and composite shapes to find their area and perimeter using appropriate formulas and units.

nodes.label: Decomposing composite shapes for area
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students decompose a composite shape into known shapes and calculate the total area by summing component areas.
nodes.minimum_width: Decompose a composite shape made of two rectangles or a rectangle and triangle; calculate total area.
nodes.typical_width: Decompose and calculate area for a range of composite shapes including those with subtracted regions (e.g. shape with a hole); select appropriate decomposition strategy.
wider: Investigate floor plan problems requiring area calculation for irregular rooms — apply to real building design contexts.
Explore shapes requiring both addition and subtraction of areas (e.g. a frame) and generalise the approach.

response_modes.reason: Decomposition requires an explicit strategy: identify the component shapes, identify dimensions from the diagram, calculate each area, combine. Students who proceed without this strategy make errors in dimension identification.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires the same dimension-identification discipline for irregular shapes — students who have not internalised the decomposition strategy in Node 1 apply it inconsistently to irregular shapes where the component boundaries are less obvious.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies a valid decomposition of the composite shape.
Combines areas correctly (adding or subtracting as required).

nodes.label: Perimeter and area of irregular shapes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students estimate and calculate the perimeter and area of irregular shapes using measurement approximation strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate the area of an irregular shape using a grid overlay; calculate perimeter by summing measured segments.
nodes.typical_width: Use increasingly accurate approximation methods (grid, line segments) to estimate area and perimeter; discuss precision and error; apply to practical contexts.
wider: Apply area estimation to a real context: estimate the area of an irregularly shaped land parcel from a map or aerial image.
Investigate how Simpson's rule or similar numerical integration methods formalise the estimation approach — preview of Y11/12 mathematics.

response_modes.reason: Irregular shape problems require judgment about appropriate estimation methods. Multiple practical contexts (land parcels, natural features, council maps) build the judgment to select appropriate precision.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real-world irregular shape problems (land parcels, ecological surveys) offer advancing students rich applied spatial reasoning — the connection to numerical integration methods is a meaningful conceptual extension.
success_criteria: Estimates the area of an irregular shape using a systematic method.
Calculates or estimates the perimeter accurately.
States the precision of the estimate and its limitations.
